title: stackward report v1
description: Output of `stackward audit --json` and `stackward probe --json`. Adding an optional field is not a breaking change; removing or renaming a field, or changing a meaning, needs report.v2. Results are ordered by group (catalog order), then check id, then subject.

generated_at.description: When the facts were collected, RFC 3339 UTC. Empty when unknown.

hostname_hash.description: sha256: plus the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the hostname. Present unless --show-hostname.

name.description: Ingress profile. mixed is inferred only (a tunnel plus public web ports) and is not a --profile value.

coverage.description: How much was actually inspected. Counts are of results, not checks.

checked.description: Results with level pass, warn, fail or info, accepted ones included.

accepted.description: Checked results a waiver accepts (also counted in checked). Absent when none.

unknown.description: Results with level unknown (could not inspect; never a pass).

root.description: Whether the audit ran as root.

summary.description: Results by level. A fail or warn result a waiver accepts is counted in accepted, not in fail or warn, so it does not trip --fail-on.

accepted.description: Fail and warn results a waiver accepts. Absent when none.

waivers.description: Every entry of the waivers file (--waivers or .stackward.yml) in file order, with what became of it. Absent when no waivers file was read.

probe.description: Present only in reports of `stackward probe`: the target as given, what it resolved to, how each address family went and every TCP connect tried.

target.description: Host name or IP address as given on the command line.

hostname.description: The --hostname checked over HTTPS, if any.

self_target.description: True when the target is the machine probe ran on (loopback or a local interface address), so the results are not an outside view. Absent otherwise.

status.description: probed, no-address (nothing to probe) or unreachable (this machine has no route to the family).

state.description: open (connected), closed (refused), filtered (no answer before the timeout), unreachable (no route from this machine) or error.

banner.description: First line the service sent, capped and reduced to printable ASCII (SSH banners).

subject.description: The exact subject of the result it accepts (redacted).

level.description: Worst result level the waiver accepts.

status.description: applied (accepted its result), long-lived (accepted its result, but expires more than a year after the audit), expired (past its date; the result is back at its level), level-exceeded (the result is worse than level, so it counts at its level), stale (no fail or warn result of the check has this subject), ambiguous (more than one result has this check and subject, so none is accepted) or unknown-check (no check has this id).

results.description: Results with this check and subject, at any level.

network.description: TCP bind and connect denied as well.

subject.description: host, container:<project>/<service>, port:<proto>/<port>, file:<path> or user:<name>.

evidence.description: Fixed set of keys per check id. Never holds secrets; redacted as a safety net.

waiver.description: Present when a waiver matches this fail or warn result. The result's level and evidence stay the real ones. accepted: counted in summary.accepted instead of its level until expires. expired: counted at its level again. level-exceeded: the result is worse than the waiver's level, so it counts at its level.

level.description: Worst result level the waiver accepts.
